data.narrative:
Vermeer, a Series A-stage Defense & Security company that has raised $10M to date, is evaluated against a universe of 10 comparables: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Stark Defence, Singularity, NODA AI, Anduril Industries, and Helsing.

Two triangulation methods apply to this valuation. Stage-progression analysis, using the $10M total raised as a proxy for post-money value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a $20M valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Stark Defence ($4.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M)—yields a median valuation of $400M, with a range of $125M to $4.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects material differences in technology maturity, customer traction, or funding velocity within the Defense & Security frontier-tech segment.

Triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $17M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $210M. The substantial gap between stage-progression ($20M) and peer-median ($400M) results reflects uncertainty around Vermeer's relative positioning within its peer cohort. Key sensitivities include which peer subset most closely mirrors Vermeer's technology roadmap and customer acquisition trajectory, and whether the company's burn rate and runway justify positioning toward the lower or upper bound of the range.
